entries.title: Bring your other articles into a chat
entries.body: In Chat, type @ and pick up to three of your other articles to bring into the conversation; the AI reads them in full along with your next question. That lets you ask how this piece relates to the others, and a citation from one of them opens that article at the passage. When you export an article, the download lists which articles each question brought in, by title, not text, and deleting an article does not remove it from chats on other articles that brought it in.

entries.title: The reading guide can search the web
entries.body: When you type to the reading guide in Chat, it can look on the web for how a piece was received, what to read alongside it, or who wrote it, and the activity line under its answer says it searched the web. This is in the typed guide only, not in the spoken Live conversation.

entries.title: Search matches by words or by meaning
entries.body: Search mode offers two ways to match, words and meaning, where it had three. Meaning shows first results as soon as you pause typing, then swaps in a more thorough search on its own, and the Find button shows it is busy rather than starting the same search twice. Saved links to the old quick option open on meaning.

entries.title: The reading guide's suggestions are easier to spot
entries.body: The reading guide's suggested actions sit under a 'Next steps' heading, with clearer buttons. Ask it about what the piece says and it can offer an 'Ask in Chat' button that starts a fresh chat with that question, one chat per press. The guide is also asked to keep its replies shorter.
